ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Best-of-eight distillation for text-to-image diffusion with a reference-matching regularizer
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion 1.5 on its own top-ranked samples. For 20000 prompts from LAION-Aesthetics, draw 8 images per prompt, keep the one with the highest aesthetic-predictor score, and train with the denoising loss on kept images plus a term that ties the fine-tuned noise predictor to the frozen reference at noise levels drawn uniformly. Train for 4000 steps with a modest learning rate. Compare against policy-gradient fine-tuning and a trajectory-divergence variant at matched numbers of gradient steps. Report reward, CLIP score, FID on COCO-30000 and a Monte Carlo estimate of the divergence from the reference on 500 prompts.
CONTROLS: DDPO with a trajectory-level divergence penalty, reward-weighted regression, an unregularized rejection-sampling run and the frozen reference; three seeds per method, plus a run with the regularizer weight set to zero.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Reward should rise by about one baseline standard deviation while FID stays within two points of the reference. It could fail if the predictor is exploited and diversity collapses, which the divergence estimate would reveal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward-filtered fine-tuning of text-to-image diffusion with score-matching regularization
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion 1.5 on the best of 4 samples per prompt, drawn for 5000 prompts from LAION-Aesthetics and scored by an aesthetic predictor; the loss is the denoising objective on kept images with a penalty on the gap between fine-tuned and frozen noise predictors. Carry the recipe over to Stable Diffusion 2.1 and SDXL, and rebuild the sample pool at several prompt-set sizes to trace how the gain depends on pool size. Report reward, CLIP score, FID on COCO-30000 and the divergence estimate for checkpoints saved at regular intervals, under a small grid of learning rates.
CONTROLS: DDPO with a trajectory-level divergence penalty, reward-weighted regression, an unregularized rejection-sampling run and the frozen reference; three seeds per backbone, plus a run with the regularizer weight set to zero.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Reward should rise by about one baseline standard deviation on each backbone while FID stays near the reference. It could fail if the predictor is exploited and diversity collapses, which the divergence estimate would reveal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward-tilted fine-tuning of a layout diffusion model on PubLayNet
PROPOSAL: Take a discrete-state layout diffusion model pre-trained on PubLayNet and tilt it toward layouts with low overlap and high alignment, using a reward calculated from bounding boxes. Sample 64 layouts per conditioning input, keep those above the batch median reward, and fine-tune on them while penalizing the per-step transition divergence from the reference at randomly chosen denoising steps. Train for 30000 steps. Evaluate overlap, alignment, FID of rendered layouts, and the fraction of generated layouts that are copies of training layouts. Compare to a reward-guided sampler that leaves the weights unchanged.
CONTROLS: Reference model without tuning, classifier-free guidance toward the reward, policy-gradient fine-tuning with trajectory divergence, and rejection sampling without the divergence term; five seeds per method, with conditional and unconditional generation reported separately.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Overlap should fall by more than a third with FID within a few points of the reference. It could fail if reward-driven tuning memorizes training layouts, which the copy fraction would expose.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-step regularized rejection sampling for graphic layouts on three datasets
PROPOSAL: Tilt a discrete-state layout diffusion model toward low overlap and high alignment with a bounding-box reward, working from the PubLayNet checkpoint and adapting it to RICO and Magazine. Sample 16 layouts per input, keep those above the median reward, and fine-tune on them with a penalty on transition divergence from the reference at chosen denoising steps. Try 3 reward weightings and 2 sampling temperatures, and evaluate overlap, alignment, FID of rendered layouts, and the fraction of generated layouts copied from training layouts after each epoch.
CONTROLS: Reference model without tuning, classifier-free guidance toward the reward, policy-gradient fine-tuning with trajectory divergence, and rejection sampling without the divergence term; five seeds per method and per dataset.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Overlap should fall by more than a third with FID near the reference on all datasets. It could fail if reward-driven tuning memorizes training layouts, which the copy fraction would expose.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Property-tilted fine-tuning of an equivariant molecule diffusion model on QM9
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a pre-trained equivariant diffusion model for 3D molecules on QM9 so that generated molecules favor a small HOMO-LUMO gap, with the gap predicted by a frozen property network. Generate a couple of thousand molecules per round, keep the best quarter, and train on them for a few hundred steps while penalizing divergence of the denoising kernel from the reference at sampled noise levels. After each of 3 rounds, report mean predicted gap, atom stability, molecule stability, validity, uniqueness and novelty, and compare with the exact tilted target on a one-dimensional toy.
CONTROLS: The untuned model with rejection filtering at sampling time, a gradient-guided sampler on the property network, and tuning without the divergence term; three seeds each, and the property network evaluated on held-out molecules.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The mean gap should shift down by roughly one standard deviation while stability stays above 95 percent of the reference. It could fail if the property network is exploited by unphysical geometries, which stability would reveal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Conditioning a 3D molecule diffusion model on quantum properties through reward reweighting
PROPOSAL: Steer a pre-trained equivariant molecule diffusion model trained on QM9 toward a small HOMO-LUMO gap predicted by a frozen property network. Generate a few hundred molecules per round, keep the best quarter, and train briefly with a penalty on divergence of the denoising kernel from the reference. Extend the same scheme to GEOM-Drugs, to the dipole moment and heat capacity, and to a spread of tilt strengths. After each round, report mean predicted gap, atom stability, molecule stability, validity, uniqueness and novelty, and fit the exact tilted target on a one-dimensional toy.
CONTROLS: The untuned model with rejection filtering at sampling time, a gradient-guided sampler on the property network, and tuning without the divergence term; three seeds each.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The mean gap should shift down by roughly one standard deviation while stability stays above 95 percent of the reference on QM9. It could fail if the property network is exploited by unphysical geometries, which stability would reveal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: SDXL reward fine-tuning with a marginal-divergence estimator versus policy gradients
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune SDXL on PickScore using rejection-sampled data from 100000 prompts of Pick-a-Pic, drawing 16 images per prompt and keeping the top two. Regularize with a Monte Carlo estimate of the marginal divergence from the reference built from the denoising-score difference at noise levels sampled by importance weights, and compare with PPO-style training under trajectory divergence and with no regularization. Train for 6000 steps at a learning rate of 1e-5. Evaluate PickScore, ImageReward, HPSv2, FID on COCO-30000, prompt-alignment accuracy on GenEval, and diversity measured by LPIPS among samples from the same prompt.
CONTROLS: PPO under trajectory divergence, unregularized rejection sampling, DPO on preference pairs, the reference SDXL, and a run that swaps the estimator weights for uniform ones; three seeds and two training lengths.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The marginal estimator should keep GenEval and FID near the reference while matching reward gains of the unregularized run. It could fail if the importance weights have heavy tails, producing unstable gradients.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Score-gap regularized rejection sampling carried to four text-to-image models
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion 1.5 on PickScore using rejection-sampled data from 20000 prompts of Pick-a-Pic, drawing 8 images per prompt and keeping the top one. Regularize with a Monte Carlo estimate of the divergence from the reference built from the denoising-score difference at noise levels sampled by importance weights. Then move the pipeline to SDXL, SD3 and PixArt, at a few regularization strengths. Evaluate PickScore, ImageReward, HPSv2, FID on COCO-30000, prompt-alignment accuracy on GenEval, and diversity measured by LPIPS among samples from the same prompt, at intermediate checkpoints.
CONTROLS: PPO under trajectory divergence, unregularized rejection sampling, DPO on preference pairs and the reference model; two seeds per backbone and per regularization strength.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The estimator should keep GenEval and FID near the reference while matching reward gains of the unregularized run on each backbone. It could fail if the importance weights have heavy tails, producing unstable gradients.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward-free correction of a pre-trained rectified flow using data samples only
PROPOSAL: Take a rectified-flow model pre-trained on ImageNet at 64 by 64 resolution and fine-tune it with a data-only objective that corrects the discretization error of the sampling ODE: simulate the ODE from noise with a coarse Euler solver, then regress the velocity field at the arrival points toward the one implied by the nearest real training images. Measure FID, precision and recall at 4, 8 and 16 function evaluations, and compare the per-sample generation time with the original model.
CONTROLS: The unmodified flow with an Euler solver and a higher-order solver, a further reflow round, consistency-style distillation, and fine-tuning on real data with no ODE simulation; three seeds, and FID calculated on 50000 samples.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: FID at 8 evaluations should drop by about 20 percent with unchanged per-sample time. It could fail if regression toward nearest images collapses diversity, visible as falling recall.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Data-driven velocity refinement of pre-trained rectified flows on four image datasets
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a rectified-flow model pre-trained on ImageNet at 64 by 64 resolution with a data-only objective: simulate the sampling ODE from noise with a coarse Euler solver, then regress the velocity field at arrival points toward the one implied by nearest real training images. Do the same for CIFAR-10, CelebA and LSUN Church, with several solver orders and simulation lengths. Measure FID, precision and recall at 4, 8 and 16 function evaluations, and compare the per-sample generation time with the original model at each fine-tuning stage.
CONTROLS: The unmodified flow with an Euler solver and a higher-order solver, reflow, consistency-style distillation, and fine-tuning on real data with no ODE simulation; two seeds per dataset.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: FID at 8 evaluations should drop by about 20 percent with unchanged per-sample time on ImageNet. It could fail if regression toward nearest images collapses diversity, visible as falling recall.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Iterated rejection-sampling fine-tuning of Stable Diffusion 3 on a mixture of rewards
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion 3 Medium over 6 rounds of rejection sampling: in each round, draw 8 images for 200000 prompts from a curated caption set, score them with a weighted mixture of aesthetic, text-rendering and object-count rewards, keep the top quarter and train on them, with the reference anchored to the previous round through a divergence penalty on the velocity field. Evaluate GenEval, T2I-CompBench, OCR accuracy on rendered text, human-preference win rate on 1000 prompts, and diversity, tracked per round.
CONTROLS: A single-round run on the same number of total samples, PPO with trajectory divergence, DPO, anchoring to the original model instead of the previous round, and the reference; two seeds and a held-out prompt set.
COST: 4200
PREDICTION: Anchoring to the previous round should beat anchoring to the original on reward while holding diversity. It could fail if errors accumulate across rounds and the policy drifts away from natural images.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Round-based rejection sampling for Stable Diffusion 3 with a velocity-field penalty
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion 3 Medium with rejection sampling in rounds: draw 8 images for 40000 prompts from a curated caption set, score them with a weighted mixture of aesthetic, text-rendering and object-count rewards, keep the top quarter and train on them, with a divergence penalty on the velocity field relative to the previous round. Run the same loop on SDXL and Flux, with a spread of reward mixtures and penalty weights. Evaluate GenEval, T2I-CompBench, OCR accuracy on rendered text, human-preference win rate on 1000 prompts, and diversity, tracked per round.
CONTROLS: A single-round run on the same number of total samples, PPO with trajectory divergence, DPO and the reference; two seeds per backbone and per reward mixture.
COST: 4200
PREDICTION: Anchoring to the previous round should beat anchoring to the original on reward while holding diversity on each backbone. It could fail if errors accumulate across rounds and the policy drifts away from natural images.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward tilting restricted to late denoising steps for document layouts
PROPOSAL: Use the multi-step structure of a pre-trained layout diffusion model by applying the reward only at the last denoising steps, where the predicted clean layout is already informative, and leaving the early steps untouched. Fine-tune a PubLayNet model by selecting, at a random late step, the best of 8 continuations from the same intermediate state, and training the denoiser on the winning continuation. Vary the starting step across 4 values and report overlap, alignment, FID and the divergence from the reference as a function of that step.
CONTROLS: Full-trajectory tilting with identical sample counts, early-step-only tilting, the untuned reference, and a reward-gradient sampler; three seeds per starting step.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Late-step tilting should reach most of the reward gain of full-trajectory tilting at lower divergence. It could fail if layout structure is fixed at early steps so that late edits change only small details.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Intermediate-state best-of-N training for layout diffusion on four datasets
PROPOSAL: Exploit the denoising chain of a pre-trained layout model by resuming sampling from one noisy layout many times and selecting the best of 8 continuations under a bounding-box reward. Fine-tune the denoiser on the winning continuation at chosen steps. Run the procedure on PubLayNet, RICO, Magazine and Crello, moving the starting step through a range of values, and report overlap, alignment, FID and the divergence from the reference as a function of that step, with a few reward weightings.
CONTROLS: Full-trajectory tilting with identical sample counts, early-step-only tilting, the untuned reference and a reward-gradient sampler; two seeds per dataset.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Resuming from intermediate states should reach most of the reward gain of full-trajectory tilting at lower divergence. It could fail if layout structure is fixed at early steps so that later edits change only small details.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stochastic-control fine-tuning of a molecule flow model with a deterministic ODE sampler
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a flow model for molecule generation on GEOM-Drugs, whose sampler is a deterministic ODE, toward a docking-score reward while preserving the marginal law relative to the reference. Convert the ODE into a stochastic process with matched marginals, then train the drift correction by regressing it toward the reward-tilted target estimated from 32 noisy continuations per state. Report docking score, validity, novelty, diversity under Tanimoto similarity, and the fitted divergence from the reference on a 2000-molecule holdout.
CONTROLS: Gradient-guided sampling, rejection sampling at the output, policy-gradient fine-tuning with trajectory divergence, and the reference flow; three seeds and a docking oracle on a different protein target as a transfer check.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Docking score should improve by about one standard deviation with novelty preserved. It could fail if the stochastic conversion alters the marginals, which the holdout divergence would reveal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Drift-correction fine-tuning of molecule flow models toward docking reward on a panel of targets
PROPOSAL: Adapt a flow model for molecule generation, whose sampler is a deterministic ODE, to docking-score rewards. Convert the ODE into a stochastic process with matched marginals, then train the drift correction by regressing toward the reward-tilted target estimated from 8 noisy continuations per state. Do this on GEOM-Drugs, QM9 and Zinc250k, for a panel of protein targets and noise schedules, and report docking score, validity, novelty, diversity under Tanimoto similarity, and the fitted divergence on a 2000-molecule holdout.
CONTROLS: Gradient-guided sampling, rejection sampling at the output, policy-gradient fine-tuning with trajectory divergence and the reference flow; two seeds per target and per noise schedule.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Docking score should improve by about one standard deviation with novelty preserved on each target. It could fail if the stochastic conversion alters the marginals, which the holdout divergence would reveal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning the initial-noise tilt jointly with the denoiser for text-to-image fine-tuning
PROPOSAL: Address the initial-noise bias of trajectory-regularized fine-tuning on Stable Diffusion 1.5 by learning, in one training loop, a small mapping that reshapes the starting Gaussian together with fine-tuned LoRA weights of the denoiser. Reward is ImageReward on 50000 captions from Pick-a-Pic, with LoRA rank 16; the regularizer compares denoising kernels only, leaving the starting distribution free. Report reward, FID, CLIP score, diversity, and the Wasserstein distance between learned and standard Gaussian starting noise, over training.
CONTROLS: Trajectory-divergence PPO with a fixed Gaussian start, noise-only optimization with frozen weights, denoiser-only tuning, and the reference; three seeds and a run with the initial reshaping removed at test time.
COST: 1600
PREDICTION: Joint learning should exceed denoiser-only tuning on reward at equal FID. It could fail if the learned start moves far from Gaussian, making samples sensitive to numerical errors.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learned starting-noise reshaping for fine-tuning four latent diffusion models
PROPOSAL: Address the initial-noise bias of trajectory-regularized fine-tuning by learning a small mapping that reshapes the starting Gaussian in one loop with LoRA weights of the denoiser. Reward is ImageReward on 10000 captions from Pick-a-Pic; the regularizer compares denoising kernels only. Apply it to Stable Diffusion 1.5, 2.1, SDXL and PixArt, scanning mapping widths and LoRA ranks, and report reward, FID, CLIP score, diversity, and the Wasserstein distance between learned and standard Gaussian starting noise at regular checkpoints.
CONTROLS: Trajectory-divergence PPO with a fixed Gaussian start, noise-only optimization with frozen weights, denoiser-only tuning and the reference; three seeds per backbone and per mapping width.
COST: 1600
PREDICTION: Joint learning should exceed denoiser-only tuning on reward at equal FID on all backbones. It could fail if the learned start moves far from Gaussian, making samples sensitive to numerical errors.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Best-of-N versus exponentially tilted targets on a Gaussian mixture diffusion
PROPOSAL: Study the relation between best-of-N sampling and the reward-tilted distribution on a two-dimensional Gaussian mixture where the denoiser is known in closed form. Train a small denoising network to match the mixture, define a reward on the mixture components, and compare four distributions: best-of-N samples for N in 2, 4, 8 and 16, the exact tilted distribution, a policy-gradient policy with trajectory divergence, and a rejection-sampling-trained policy. Report the divergence between each and the exact tilt, estimated from 100000 samples by kernel density.
CONTROLS: Closed-form tilted density as ground truth, a bin-count estimator as a cross-check for the kernel one, and ten seeds for each trained policy.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Best-of-N should match a tilt of strength growing with the logarithm of N, and the rejection-trained policy should sit nearer the tilt than the trajectory-divergence policy. It could fail if the two-dimensional setting hides high-dimensional effects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tilted-target comparison on Gaussian mixtures of growing dimension
PROPOSAL: Examine how best-of-N sampling relates to the reward-tilted distribution on Gaussian mixtures whose denoiser is known in closed form, going from 2 to 128 dimensions. A small denoising network is trained on each mixture, a reward is defined on its components, and best-of-N samples for N up to 64 are set against the exact tilted distribution, a policy-gradient policy with trajectory divergence, and a policy trained by rejection sampling. Estimate the divergence from the exact tilt with kernels and with bins.
CONTROLS: Closed-form tilted density as ground truth, a bin-count estimator as a cross-check for the kernel one, and five seeds for each trained policy at each dimension.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Best-of-N should match a tilt of strength growing with the logarithm of N at every dimension, and the rejection-trained policy should sit nearer the tilt than the trajectory-divergence policy. It could fail if estimation error grows with dimension.
